A few years ago when my grandmother finally had to be placed in a nursing home I offered to help my mother during the transition. She was already in denial that she needed to prepare for my grandmother's funeral, so I knew this wasn't going to happen, but I tried. I told her she had two options with the house. Hire a pest control guy and get some relatives to help her deal with the bed bugs. Or turn off the utilities and hire a plumber to shut off the water until such a time as the bed bugs all starved to death and she could move into the house.

She gets the wild crazy eyes that cues that she's trying to shut down her amygdala and immediately asks me if I would find a plumber for her, which I refuse. I tell her point blankly, "sparing you a forty mile round trip to make sure the mailbox is empty to not attract burglars is enough of a favor from me." So, for eighteen months afterwards she doesn't bother with finding a plumber at all. I casually press the issue as the summer begins to come to a close and the temperatures begin to drop, but she keeps saying like money's tight, which was bull, but I moved on as I'm not paying for this.

Then I get a phone call on a Tuesday evening from my mother telling me one of my grandmothers neighbors noticed water coming from under my grandmothers house. I tell her I'm no plumber, get one of our castrate cousins to check and not to bother me for help until she had money for a plumber. Wouldn't you know it, the very next day she's got money to hire a plumber and now she's begging me to help her. So, I tell her I'll be at my grandmothers to help her Friday evening. Yea, I let the plumbing leak an additional two days because I had those few fucks to give.

It was pure dumb luck that she called that evening and got my mother at all. In the end, my mother had to pay two thousand dollars just to repair the three burst water mains on what was still fairly new home plumbing.
